Subject: Post-deploy: v4.2 (int8) upgrade — p99 jump & 502 wave

Jonas —

We kicked the v4.2 + int8 rollout at 07:00 PT (canary -> 50% traffic) and immediately saw p99 jump from ~120ms to ~620ms and a 502/timeout wave from 07:08–07:25. The customer-facing API (checkout/price) is affected; customers are reporting timeouts.

Attached: diagnostic_snapshot.json (small), p99_trace_snippet.html (snippet from our tracing).

Quick data:
- Error rate: baseline 0.2% -> observed 3.6% (5xx & timeouts)
- Throughput: attempted burst, many requests retried causing queueing
- Region: us-west-2 primary

We rolled canary back at 07:30 which reduced errors but p99 remains ~280–320ms for some paths. Can you advise on Redwood-side mitigations (fallback to float16 variant, routing to Dedicated pool, or immediate full rollback)? TeleZest needs a one-paragraph exec summary for their CTO within the hour.

Thanks,
Claire
Product Ops — TeleZest

Claire — thank you for the quick heads up and artifacts. I see the traces; there are two signals that look like root causes: the int8 kernel path is hitting a slower fallback on some sequence patterns (KV-cache memory shuffles) and the continuous-batching window expanded under retry churn — that magnified latency.

Immediate plan (next 90m):
- Rishi / Runtime: roll a soft fallback policy to route traffic to the v4.2 float16 variant for the affected route (/checkout/price) — this should bring p99 back within SLO while preserving the model version.
- Olga / Quant ops: revert the int8 qprofile for TeleZest only (config override) if routing doesn't return p99 <200ms in 20m.
- Marissa / Customer: I'll draft the exec summary for their CTO, include rollback options and expected timeline.

Claire — please grant us write access to the perf traces link if you want deeper kernel traces (we have the telemetry hooks that correlate sequence shapes to kernel selection).

I’ll update in 20 minutes with an ops snapshot.

— Jonas
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

Looping in a quick tech summary + action items from runtime side.

Observations:
- TeleZest traffic has a high variance of short+long sequences (checkout meta + user notes). On int8 we see an increased rate of kernel fallback to the "sparse attention emulation" path for certain prompt shapes — that code path has higher per-token latency.
- Continuous-batching window increased from 8ms -> ~24ms during retry storms which pushed queuing latency.
- Retries from client (3x) compounded CPU-side scheduling; we saw 30% increased CPU on the host pinned to that slice.

Immediate ops:
1) Traffic split: we applied a route override pushing 80% of /checkout/price to float16 v4.2 variant at 09:00Z (should be live now).
2) Telemetry: asked SRE to kick perf traces for the int8 path and provided a pre-built metric query (RWI-2841).
3) Rollback guard: if float16 split does not cut p99 <200ms in 12m, we will schedule a full config rollback to v4.1 for TeleZest with 30m notice.

Attachments: short diagnostic snapshot extracted from host (attached).

Rishi
Principal Engineer, Runtime

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Claire Huang <claire@telezest.ai>, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-09T14:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-deploy: v4.2 (int8) upgrade — p99 jump & 502 wave

Claire / Rajiv — finalizing the one-paragraph exec note for your CTO and a recommended path forward. Please feel free to copy/paste.

Executive summary (for TeleZest CTO):
At 07:00 PT TeleZest was on-boarded to Redwood model v4.2 with an int8 quantization profile. Following canary expansion we observed a rapid increase in p99 latency and 502 responses due to an interaction between the int8 kernel fallback for specific sequence shapes and amplified continuous-batching windows caused by client retries. Redwood applied a targeted routing override to direct the affected endpoint to the v4.2 float16 variant and disabled the int8 qprofile for TeleZest as a guarded rollback. Early results show p99 reduced to ~180ms and error rate back to ~0.4%.

Recommended next steps:
- Short-term (now): keep routing to float16 for 24–48 hours while we run a focused qprofile regression test against TeleZest prompt corpus (Redwood will execute).
- Mid-term (72h): if int8 cannot be made stable for TeleZest’s shape distribution, consider keeping float16 for their workload and apply a gradual re-onboarding with smaller canary steps and synthetic prompts that match TeleZest traffic.
- Ops ask: Redwood requests continued trace access and a small sample dataset (anonymized) of TeleZest request shapes to reproduce locally.

Logistics: Redwood will file a follow-up report (RWI-2841) with timelines and results. We estimate a rollback window if needed = 30 minutes.

Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success — Redwood Inference

On behalf of the ops team — Jonas, Rishi, Olga
